A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E2H Reasoner work. Their complete main texts, appendices, figures, tables and equations support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM post-training experiments on five reasoning benchmarks, including task-decomposition, scheduling and SFT comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Self-Evolve comparisons, difficulty-split sensitivity results and training-sample accounting.

M1.justification: Task decomposition, cosine and Gaussian scheduling, reward design, and GRPO with LoRA remain unchanged. The expanded difficulty-estimation explanation in Section 3.1 describes procedures already documented in v1's experiments and appendix.

E1.justification: Both versions use Blocksworld, Countdown, MATH, GSM8K and AQuA with the same task coverage and OOD scenarios. The new difficulty-grouping experiment repartitions retained data rather than introducing another task or population.

E2.justification: v2 adds Self-Evolve, an adaptive curriculum comparator, across all three models on Blocksworld, Countdown and MATH, and across GSM8K and AQuA for Qwen 1.5B (Tables 3, 4 and 9). This substantially extends comparisons beyond the retained fixed curriculum, uniform sampling, CoT and SFT baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix G.3 adds GSM8K evaluations using three and five difficulty groups alongside the existing four-group configuration. Appendix B introduces difficulty-specific sample accounting under a fixed training budget. Previously reported training hyperparameters and decoding settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds two focused analyses: sensitivity to the number of difficulty groups (Table 12) and training-sample allocation by difficulty (Table 5). Existing task-decomposition ablations, Gaussian-parameter comparisons and scheduling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 newly states that results are averaged across three seeds; v1 gives no corresponding seed count. This is new reporting, not evidence that the number of runs increased. No dispersion estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds Self-Evolve results, sample counts and split-count sensitivity scores. Reported E2H-G Countdown Hard/OOD scores change from 28.1/14.2 to 41.0/19.2 for Qwen 1.5B, and from 43.5/19.4 to 60.7/32.3 for Qwen 3B in the corresponding summary tables. However, v2's SFT and Gaussian-detail tables retain earlier values, so these are unreconciled reporting changes rather than established performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, sample-efficiency condition and Appendix A proofs are substantively unchanged. Replacing the performance-loss symbol L_K with E_K aligns notation without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that probabilistic easy-to-hard curricula improve small-model reasoning and generalization, with convergence guarantees and conditional sample-efficiency advantages. Although the abstract drops its closing empirical summary, those claims remain elsewhere in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation that targeting 50% solve rates may provide insufficient foundational mastery, and qualifies adaptive-curriculum benefits as dataset dependent. Appendix B newly interprets hard-example counts as sample-efficiency evidence. The limitations discussion expands on nonadaptive scheduling but removes v1's explicit acknowledgment that larger models were not tested.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address, explicitly reports an effective batch size of eight and 12,800 training samples for Appendix B, and states that Self-Evolve uses its authors' hyperparameters without enumerating them. Existing hardware, training-time, GRPO, LoRA and inference details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al.'s Self-Evolving Curriculum, Foster et al.'s Frontier of Learnability and Bercovich et al.'s Llama-Nemotron, sharpening positioning against adaptive and fixed-stage curricula. The Chen–Maguluri reference changes from preprint to publication metadata but represents the same theoretical source.

P1.justification: There are selective rewrites of the introduction, curriculum discussion, task-decomposition explanation and results. v2 adopts author-year citations, separates the conclusion from appendix limitations, and reorganizes supplementary analyses into subsections. The main narrative and most methodological and theoretical prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document-wide title, heading and running-header design and substantially redistributes displays. It splits v1's Table 3, moving Qwen 3B results into appendix Table 9, adds sample-count and sensitivity tables, relocates Figure 2, and revises captions and ranking emphasis. The six existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Self-Evolve comparisons, split-count tests and three-seed disclosure improve empirical scrutiny. However, v2's Qwen 3B Countdown Hard/OOD scores are 60.7/32.3 in Table 9 versus 43.5/19.4 in Table 10; v1's corresponding entries agreed. These conflicting values change whether E2H-G beats Self-Evolve's 56.8/29.3. Appendix B also uses fewer hard examples at an unchanged 12,800-total budget to support sample-efficiency claims without demonstrating total-sample savings. The useful additions and new reliability problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
